title: TUBB4A mutations result in both glial and neuronal degeneration in an H-ABC leukodystrophy mouse model
abstract: Mutations in TUBB4A result in a spectrum of leukodystrophy including Hypomyelination with Atrophy of Basal Ganglia and Cerebellum (H-ABC), a rare hypomyelinating leukodystrophy, often associated with a recurring variant p.Asp249Asn (D249N). We have developed a novel knock-in mouse model harboring heterozygous ( Tubb4a ) and the homozygous ( D249N/+ Tubb4a ) mutation that recapitulate the progressive motor dysfunction with tremor, dystonia and ataxia seen in H-ABC. D249N/D249N Tubb4a mice have myelination deficits along with dramatic decrease in mature oligodendrocytes and their progenitor cells. Additionally, a significant loss occurs in the cerebellar granular neurons and striatal neurons in D249N/D249N Tubb4a mice. In vitro studies show decreased survival and dysfunction in microtubule dynamics in neurons from D249N/D249N Tubb4a mice. Thus D249N/D249N Tubb4a mice demonstrate the complex cellular physiology of H-ABC, likely due to independent effects on oligodendrocytes, striatal neurons, and cerebellar granule cells in the context of altered microtubule dynamics, with profound neurodevelopmental deficits.
